facts.text: The README says the code sends and requests information from an SR830 lock-in amplifier
The README says the code is written in a sequential fashion and is to be updated to object-oriented code
The only third-party import is pyserial (import serial)
ask_device opens /dev/ttyUSB0 at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit and a 0.1 s timeout
ask_device encodes the command as text, writes and flushes it, reads one line and decodes it as UTF-8
set_device opens the same port, writes and flushes the encoded command, closes the port and reads no reply
Commands are newline-terminated text (ask_device('PHAS?\n'))
PHAS? queries the reference phase shift
FREQ? queries the reference frequency
FREQ sets the reference frequency when the source is internal and accepts 0.001 to 102000 Hz
SLVL? queries the sine output amplitude
SLVL sets the sine output amplitude and accepts 0.004 to 5.000
OUTP? returns X for index 1, Y for 2, R for 3 and theta for 4
ISRC sets the input configuration to 0, 1, 2 or 3
IGND sets the input shield grounding to 0 or 1
ICPL sets the input coupling to 0 or 1
ILIN sets the line notch filter to 0, 1, 2 or 3
RMOD sets the reserve mode to 0, 1 or 2
OFLT selects one of the 20 time-constant indexes of the set_tau table, 0 for 10 us through 19 for 30 ks
OFSL sets the low-pass filter slope to 0, 1 or 2
SYNC sets the synchronous filter to 0 or 1
*IDN? queries the device identification string
set_phas sends FREQ instead of PHAS, so the clone has no working phase write command
set_aux_inp builds the AUXV command with ++, which raises TypeError when called
